chunks: Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah ibn Muḥammad ibn 'Īsā narrated to me from his father, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Jamīl ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Fuḍayl ibn Yasar, from Abū Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Ziyārah (visitation) of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) equals a purified Ḥajj with the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family).
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Ibn Qulawayh in *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, elevates the Ziyārah of Imam al-Ḥusayn (a.s.) to the status of a Hajj performed in the direct presence of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.), highlighting the unique spiritual proximity granted to the Ahl al-Bayt. In Shia scholarly tradition, this equivalence underscores the continuity of prophetic authority and the centrality of Karbala in Islamic piety, suggesting that visiting the martyr’s grave carries the weight of a major act of worship. The comparison to *Hajj al-Mabrūr* (accepted pilgrimage) further implies that such a visit, when performed with sincerity, serves as a means of expiation and spiritual elevation comparable to the pinnacle of Sunni and Shia devotional practice.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 6. Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Jamīl ibn Sāliḥ, from Fuďayl ibn Yasār, who said: Abū Ja’far (Imam Bāqir (a.s.)) said:
Going to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) is equal to performing a purified Hajj with the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.).
